elements.content: Communication Goal: I can exchange greetings, introduce myself, and ask for basic personal details.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 1. Nice to meet you!
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Nice to meet you!
- Materials: Name badges, dialogue cards, world map, COSYmanuals 'to be' and 'question words' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• exchange social greetings and polite introductions
• ask partners for basic personal details
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles A0 greetings and 'to be'.

Next lesson: Lesson 2 recycles personal details to talk about nationality and origin.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

nice — pleasant or kind. Example: She is a nice person.
fine — well or okay. Example: I am fine, thank you.
thank — to say you are grateful. Example: Thank you for your help.
name — the word people use to call you. Example: My name is Sara.
hello — a greeting when you meet someone. Example: Hello, my name is Alex.
goodbye — a word you say when you leave. Example: Goodbye, see you tomorrow.
meet — to see and speak to someone. Example: Nice to meet you.
how are you — a friendly question about someone's state. Example: Hello, how are you?
and you — a short return question. Example: I am fine. And you?
friend — a person you like and know well. Example: Tom is my best friend.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Nice to meet you. (polite introduction)
• How are you? (asking about someone)
• I'm fine, thanks. (polite answer)
• And you? (returning the question)
• What's your name? (asking for a name)
• Goodbye, see you soon. (polite goodbye)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'pleasant or kind'?
Which word means 'well or okay'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Polite intonation and the /aɪ/ sound in 'nice'

nice /naɪs/ — long /aɪ/
fine /faɪn/ — long /aɪ/
thank /θæŋk/ — voiceless th
goodbye /ɡʊdˈbaɪ/ — stress the second syllable
Listen and repeat:
Nice to meet you. How are you? I'm fine, thanks. And you?

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be' to say who someone is, how they feel, and where they are from.

Form:
The verb 'to be': I am / You are / He, she, it is / We are / They are. Negative: I'm not, isn't, aren't. Question: Am I...? Are you...? Is he...?

Examples:
• I am a student.
• She is from Spain.
• We are happy today.
• They are not teachers.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My name ___ Alex.
They ___ from Italy.
I ___ tired today.
She ___ not a teacher.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am ... (a student / happy / from Egypt).
• She is ... (a teacher / tired / from Spain).
• They are ... (students / at home / happy).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
• Is she from France? — Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
• Are they happy? — Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write two true sentences with 'I am...' and 'I am not...'.
• Introduce two people in the class with 'He/She is...'.
Reading: Nice to meet you!

Nice to meet you! My name is David. I am from Canada. How are you? I am fine, thanks. And you? I am fine too. What is your name? My name is Anna. Where are you from? I am from Poland. It is nice to meet you, Anna. Goodbye, see you soon!
Where is David from?
What is the woman's name?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Hello. Nice to meet you.
B: Nice to meet you too. I'm Anna.
A: I'm David. How are you?
B: I'm fine, thanks. And you?
A: I'm fine. Where are you from?
B: I'm from Poland.
What is the man's name?
Where is Anna from?
Speaking task: Introduce yourself to three classmates. Ask their names, where they are from, and how they are.

• How do you greet a new colleague?
• What do you say when you meet someone for the first time?
• How do you say goodbye politely?
• Do you shake hands when you meet someone?
• What is a good first question?
Role-play: You are at an international conference. Meet three people and exchange basic personal details.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a short introduction (5–6 sentences) with your name, country, and a polite question.
Model: Hello! My name is ... I am from ... Nice to meet you. How are you?
